name: Prof. Wei-Ling Chen
title: Associate Professor
bio: Works on why large language models fail silently on inputs just outside their training distribution, and how to build evaluation harnesses that catch it before deployment.
contact_style: Prefers a short email that references a specific paper or project of theirs, not a generic introduction.

name: Prof. Ramesh Kumar
title: Assistant Professor
bio: Builds RL agents that keep working when the environment quietly changes underneath them — factory robots, not just game benchmarks.
contact_style: Open to cold emails from students who've taken at least one ML module.

name: Prof. Hui-Min Tan
title: Professor
bio: Applies vision models to early detection in medical scans, working closely with a teaching hospital's radiology department.
contact_style: Lab is full this semester — worth checking back next semester.

name: Prof. Lars Eriksen
title: Associate Professor
bio: Studies how people actually use AI copilots in creative work, and where the interface gets in the way of trust.
contact_style: Runs a public sign-up sheet each semester rather than reading cold emails.

name: Prof. Aisha Rahman
title: Assistant Professor
bio: Works on telling apart correlation and causation in large observational health datasets, with an eye on methods practitioners can actually use.
contact_style: Prefers students bring a specific dataset or question, not just an interest in 'AI'.

name: Prof. Daniel Ong
title: Professor
bio: Builds the infrastructure layer that makes large model training and serving fast and cheap — not the models themselves, the plumbing under them.
contact_style: Wants to see a GitHub link with real systems code, not just coursework.

name: Prof. Meera Pillai
title: Assistant Professor
bio: Focuses on making generative models work well in Southeast Asian languages that big labs mostly ignore.
contact_style: Especially interested in students who speak a Southeast Asian language beyond English.

name: Prof. Jonathan Teo
title: Associate Professor
bio: Studies how early-stage tech startups actually decide what to build first, and advises a handful of student founding teams each year.
contact_style: Prefers students bring a real (even half-formed) startup idea rather than a generic RA request.

name: Prof. Grace Lim
title: Assistant Professor
bio: Works on the math underneath why deep learning training actually converges, and when it doesn't.
contact_style: Expects a strong grade in a theory-heavy module before considering an RA request.

name: Prof. Farid Hassan
title: Professor
bio: Researches methods for understanding what large models are actually doing internally, motivated by safety before capability.
contact_style: High-demand lab — RA slots usually go to students who've already done a related independent project.
